what: Deliverable 1 of the design reset: which previous decisions constrain the new design. Nothing is deleted. Every record named here stays where it is.
privacy: Tyler's private ruling notes are cited by date and paraphrased. Quotes come only from files already in this repository, from the reset directive, and from one requirement relayed by the Coordinator.

currentRequirements.paraphrase: Old decisions inform the review and do not decide it.
currentRequirements.words: Previous decisions should inform the review, but they should not dictate its conclusions.
Start with the intended player experience, not the current implementation.
Old numerical balance targets are hypotheses, not binding requirements.

currentRequirements.paraphrase: A fresh math foundation, with model families compared.
currentRequirements.words: Do not begin with current damage formulas and simply adjust coefficients.

currentRequirements.paraphrase: Shared mechanics, no new hard-coded exceptions.
currentRequirements.words: Do not create new hardcoded exceptions to force isolated content into balance.

currentRequirements.paraphrase: Every system must earn its place.
currentRequirements.words: They must earn their place in the new design.

currentRequirements.paraphrase: Redesign before balancing. No detailed numbers before the systems are validated.
currentRequirements.words: Do not lock detailed numerical rulings before validating the systems that produce those numbers.

currentRequirements.paraphrase: Approval by design package. An agent choosing an option does not make it final.
currentRequirements.words: Do not mark design decisions finalized simply because an agent has selected an option.

currentRequirements.paraphrase: No gameplay changes until the seven deliverables are reviewed.
currentRequirements.words: Do not implement gameplay changes yet.

currentRequirements.paraphrase: Keep every old decision as a record.
currentRequirements.words: Preserve them as historical records. Do not delete them.

currentRequirements.paraphrase: A recommendation is not a fact because a document holds it.
currentRequirements.words: Do not let a previous recommendation become a fact simply because it appears in a design document.

currentRequirements.paraphrase: Gear may carry randomization where it adds decisions. Flat percent upgrades alone are not enough. This supersedes fixed stats for each item (IT-1).
currentRequirements.words: Im totally cool with adding bits of randomization to gear if it makes the game more dynamic/more decisions to be made. Everything just being +x percent stronger feels dull, we need something deeper and more exciting when rare drops occur

assumptions.paraphrase: Multiplayer only, online only and server-authoritative. The client sends intents and draws the state the server returns.

where: every RPC and the hr-accrue engine

assumptions.reason: It makes the world shared and the economy unforgeable. The reset questions no part of it, and the design brief of the same day lists it as identity.

words.text: The client never authors anything.
A server-authoritative simulation.

assumptions.paraphrase: No client-side solo progression tier. It was rejected three times.
assumptions.reason: It follows from FR-1. It is a rule about authority and offline play in the browser. It is not a ruling that solo play is second class, and it must not be read as one.

assumptions.paraphrase: Hunts keep running on the server after the browser closes. A session is needed only to start or change a hunt.

where: the world tick and the settle

assumptions.reason: This is the idle half of the game. The reset asks how to make automated hunting interesting, which takes it as given.

words.text: Hunts keep running on the server after the browser closes

assumptions.paraphrase: The server owns anything tradeable, rankable or contributable, with clamps, a server clock and an append-only ledger. Row security is per user.

where: the Security review before Early Access

assumptions.reason: A genuine limit of a shared economy. It shapes how a system is built and never which system is chosen.

assumptions.paraphrase: No back-compat, no save migration, and a wipe at the Early Access launch.
assumptions.reason: It is what makes a ground-up redesign affordable. It removes a constraint and adds none.

words.text: Design correctly, not compatibly.

assumptions.paraphrase: Steam and desktop first, built for mobile from one web core, with phones in landscape and windows as sheets.
assumptions.reason: A platform limit. It bounds screens and never systems.

assumptions.paraphrase: The north star: a large multiplayer semi-idle game with a shared live world, on clean code.
assumptions.reason: It is the one-line definition of the game and nothing in the reset moves it.

words.text: a large-scale multiplayer semi-idle game with a shared live world

assumptions.paraphrase: Balance is fixed at the formula layer. One framework for each kind of mechanic, and no ground, weapon or monster gets math of its own.
assumptions.reason: The reset says it again in its own words, so it is a current requirement. One part of the older brief does lose authority: its line that approved design is to be preserved.

words.text: My goal is to build a mathematically consistent, formula-driven MMORPG, not a collection of individually balanced hunting grounds, spells, monsters, weapons, and exceptions.
Use shared mechanics instead of arbitrary content-specific exceptions.

assumptions.paraphrase: The formula audit was told to preserve approved design and flag conflicts to Tyler.
assumptions.reason: This line is why the formula work cleaned the old math up and did not compare model families. The reset asks for the comparison.

assumptions.paraphrase: Automated hunting with meaningful character preparation. The decisions live in builds, gear, ground choice, bar rules, resources and plans.
assumptions.reason: Stated as identity on 2026-11-21 and taken as given by the reset.

words.text: Automated hunting with meaningful character preparation.
What makes automated hunting strategically interesting?

assumptions.paraphrase: Character Levels never end.
assumptions.reason: Stated as identity and taken as given by the reset. The curve itself is LP-1 and keeps no authority.

words.text: Unlimited character progression.
What makes progression rewarding across unlimited levels?

assumptions.paraphrase: Distinct combat styles with no rigid vocations.
assumptions.reason: The reset asks what makes styles distinct, so styles stay. Which styles, weapons and skills exist is open (HE-4, CO-4, CO-7).

words.text: Distinct combat styles without rigid vocations.
What makes different combat styles meaningfully distinct?

assumptions.paraphrase: A deep gear chase with rare finds.
assumptions.reason: Taken as given by the reset. Tiers, rates and upgrade systems are open (IT-2 to IT-10).

words.text: Deep equipment progression and rare drops.
What makes equipment acquisition exciting?

assumptions.paraphrase: Solo play is worthwhile and party play is compelling.

where: book 00 section 3.2, which reads the opposite way: no solo or group targets

assumptions.reason: The reset asks both questions as equals. The overhaul treats a lone hero as the slower choice and drops every party-size target (HE-3). The two cannot both stand, and the reset is newer.

words.text: Solo viability alongside rewarding four-character parties.
What makes solo play worthwhile?
What makes party play compelling?

assumptions.paraphrase: A persistent economy driven by players.
assumptions.reason: Taken as given by the reset. Sinks, prices and the market shape are open.

words.text: A persistent, player-driven economy.
What creates a sustainable economy?

assumptions.paraphrase: Crafting, housing, collections and long-term goals are part of the game.
assumptions.reason: The brief lists them as identity. The reset, later the same day, lists crafting professions, housing and the Bestiary among systems that must earn their place. Long-term goals stay. The named systems are open.

assumptions.paraphrase: The game stays meaningful over thousands of hours.
assumptions.reason: Stated as identity and repeated by the reset.

words.text: Systems that remain meaningful over thousands of hours.
What should make Hearthrise compelling for thousands of hours?

assumptions.paraphrase: Tibia and Huntera inspire mechanics only. Never their names, sprites, maps, screens or text.
assumptions.reason: A legal limit. It applies to any design.

words.text: Tibia and Huntera inspire mechanics only, never names, sprites, maps, UI or text.

assumptions.paraphrase: The creative standards: handcrafted, no filler names, every system passes the purpose test, every item has a source and a use.
assumptions.reason: The purpose test is the same test the reset asks for. It is a standard for judging a design and it prescribes no system.

words.text: More systems is not a better game.
Do not mistake adding features for improving gameplay.

assumptions.source: the balance ruling of 2026-10-25, cited in tests/level-curve.mjs
assumptions.paraphrase: Progress is deliberately slow and old-school, with frequent smaller rewards on the way.
assumptions.reason: A feel he chose for the old game. It may well survive, but it is a preference to confirm, and the table built on it is a hypothesis.

assumptions.paraphrase: One account for each player, with up to four heroes playing at once in separate character sessions.
assumptions.reason: The number four came from the old client rebuild. It now sets the unit of play for every system, and nobody has compared it with one hero or with another party model on equal terms.

assumptions.paraphrase: All four heroes from the first day, with no slot prices.

where: lane FB-5, built, with staged migrations 1036 to 1039
CE-4, CE-5, CE-10, GR-79 and GR-80

assumptions.reason: His own decision on the day of the reset, made to end an argument about slot prices inside the old design. It is the largest single shape in the book. Confirm it inside the party package before anything else rests on it.

assumptions.paraphrase: The four together beat the same four split up. No balance targets for solo or group play. Party XP is paid by size alone.

where: six dropped bands (P6.2 to P7.4) in tools/balance-program/standards.mjs

assumptions.reason: The reset asks for targets across solo play and party play, and asks what makes solo play worthwhile. That reverses this ruling in plain words.

assumptions.paraphrase: The role comes from the weapon in hand. Six starter weapon sets, any hero can switch, and tank is a job of a melee hero with a shield.
assumptions.reason: The idea of styles without vocations is identity (ID-3). This is one way to build it. Others exist, and none was compared.

assumptions.paraphrase: Hunting is instanced, alone or as a party of four at most. Towns, chat and trade are the shared part.

where: the engine, where heroes cannot stand on the enemy side in 93 places across 22 modules (the MM-41 check)
MM-2, MM-20 and MM-48, each shaped so every fight stays one party of four

assumptions.reason: Tyler asked on 2026-11-21 about shared areas for eight. The study answered inside the present engine and MM-20 chose a presence strip. A fresh architecture should weigh it on design value first and engine cost second.

assumptions.paraphrase: Party rules: Level XP split evenly, the party leaves together, own heroes join at once, loot split by gold value and a rotating roll for a Rare.
assumptions.reason: Rules written for the old party model. They follow whatever party design is chosen.

assumptions.paraphrase: Party XP is one table by size and by how many weapon ways the party holds. A lone hero gets a bonus.

where: tests/party-class-xp-line.mjs, which still holds the rule the overhaul itself dropped

assumptions.reason: A guard still fails on a target that GR-3 already removed. It shows how an old ruling outlives its own reversal in code.

assumptions.paraphrase: On-call heroes: another account may hire a hero for a window, on a separate hire stamina pool, for a small cut of XP.
assumptions.reason: His own typed design, written as a fix to the old party model. It belongs in the party package as one option.

assumptions.paraphrase: The home, Storage, gold purse and farm are shared by the account. The Bestiary is kept for each hero.
assumptions.reason: Consequences of the four-hero account. They move with HE-1.

assumptions.paraphrase: One combat engine runs every hunt, viewed or not, and is the same online and offline.

where: the balance tools, which run the same engine

assumptions.reason: It keeps offline hunts honest and makes a simulation true. The reset asks for one shared authoritative model, which is this rule.

words.text: Test complete gameplay scenarios, using a shared authoritative mathematical model.

assumptions.paraphrase: The engine as built: src/core/combat-sim.js, a 10 second settle and 100 millisecond steps.

where: the world-tick parity rule in section 3.3b

assumptions.reason: A fact about today's code written into the rules file as an invariant. A new math model may keep it, but it should be a result and not a premise.

assumptions.paraphrase: The damage and defense family as built: a hit is skill plus gear, a swing rolls 1 to Power, mitigation stops at 60%, and the order is dodge, absorb, resist, ward.

where: GR-11, GR-12, GR-13, GR-23, CORE-3 and CORE-4

assumptions.reason: Every combat row of the overhaul adjusts this family and none compares another. The reset forbids starting from current formulas and adjusting coefficients.

assumptions.paraphrase: Four uncapped combat skills (Melee, Ranged, Magic, Defense) plus Inner Flame, and gathering and crafting skills capped at 99.
assumptions.reason: The skill list was copied forward. The reset names skills among the things that must earn their place.

assumptions.paraphrase: A basic attack takes 2.0 seconds for every hero and every monster.
assumptions.reason: One fixed number that removes attack speed as a lever. The reset wants every lever looked at.

assumptions.paraphrase: Armor weights: heavy absorbs and adds health, medium dodges, light wards and adds mana. Mixed sets blend with no penalty.
assumptions.reason: A defense design made for the old math. It is one candidate for the new one.

assumptions.paraphrase: The weapon ways and their jobs: sword and shield tanks and levels slowly alone on purpose, axes bleed, the hammer crushes, bow, crossbow, wand, staff, and fists as the all-rounder.
assumptions.reason: Content of the old game. Each way must earn its place.

assumptions.paraphrase: The spell and rune set: runes fuel spells only, nine rune families, sixteen Necrotic and Storm spells planned, and a list of ruled spell details.
assumptions.reason: The reset says not to assume existing spells survive. This is the largest block of content carried forward by ruling alone.

assumptions.paraphrase: How skills train: Magic on mana spent, Melee and Ranged on damage, Defense on blows taken. A blow never reads the hero's own Level.
assumptions.reason: Training rules of the old skill set. They move with CO-4.

assumptions.paraphrase: No immunities, only percentages. No stagger. Weakness and resistance sit in monster data.
assumptions.reason: Reasonable rules, each made to fix one report. Monster mechanics are on the reset's review list.

assumptions.paraphrase: The bar as built: two rows of ten slots, up to three conditions a slot, slot order is priority, and the tank casts Challenge by itself.
assumptions.reason: That preparation is the play is identity (ID-1). This layout is one build of it.

assumptions.paraphrase: Every formula is public in an in-game wiki.
assumptions.reason: It fits the reset's wish for simple shared math, but he has not said it again. Confirm it in the math package.

assumptions.paraphrase: Three tiers for each ground: Normal, Dangerous and Deadly. A tier is a percent dial on XP and difficulty, never on gold, and it sets the pull.
assumptions.reason: The whole risk design hangs on this three-step dial. Hunting ground mechanics are on the review list.

assumptions.paraphrase: One difficulty for every group size, the same monsters for everyone, and no hunt shaped for profit by party size.
assumptions.reason: He said this many times and with force. It is still a rule of the old game, so it is a strong preference to confirm.

assumptions.paraphrase: The danger bands: Normal kills at most once in 1,000 hours, and Deadly kills a mid-geared party 50 to 100 times in 1,000 hours at every Level.
assumptions.reason: Targets set before the systems that produce them. The reset calls these hypotheses.

assumptions.paraphrase: A death costs 6% of all Level XP and 6% of combat skill progress, can take a Level, and Blessings cut it by 25, 50 and 75%. A ladder of more Blessings opens at high Levels.

where: CLAUDE.md section 6, as a persistence invariant

assumptions.reason: A tuning number written into the rules file. The critical review found nobody had counted the hours a death costs an idle party.

assumptions.paraphrase: Nothing refuses a Level. A ground's Level is a guide and a big risk shows a warning.
assumptions.reason: A clear player-freedom preference. Confirm it with the hunting package.

assumptions.paraphrase: Monster tuning calls: a little more health and damage everywhere, area spells as the wall of the harder tiers, and boss fights with phases.
assumptions.reason: Single-lever fixes to the old numbers. The reset asks to stop solving problems with one variable.

assumptions.paraphrase: A death ends the hunt and sends the hero to town. No knockouts, no falls and no resume.
assumptions.reason: A rule of the old death design, written into the rules file. It moves with TD-4.

assumptions.paraphrase: The Level table of hunted hours is the law and XP is derived from it: Level 10 in 6 hours, 50 in 168, 100 in 600 and 400 in 4,580.

where: bands P1, P2, P11, P12 and P13
GR-5, GR-6, GR-6a, GR-6b and GR-6d

assumptions.reason: The most binding number in the book. Kill pay, gear steps, prices, death cost and content runway are all counted in its hours. Its own source called it a goal to validate.

assumptions.paraphrase: Every time number assumes a player hunts 12 hours a hero a day, measured in low, mid and best gear at 31 Levels up to 400.

where: CLOCK, CHECKPOINTS and GRID in standards.mjs
every day count in the book

assumptions.reason: A measuring convention chosen for the old plan. A new plan may keep it, but as a choice.

assumptions.paraphrase: The pace seat is a mid-geared four on Dangerous.
assumptions.reason: It ties the Level clock to the four-hero party. It falls with HE-2 and HE-3 if those change.

assumptions.paraphrase: Levels 1 to 50 are timed on a lone new hero, with Level 10 in 6 hours and no early Level over 2 hours.
assumptions.reason: Its stated evidence is two real players who quit. That is a lead and not a measurement.

assumptions.paraphrase: Best gear is about 15% faster and takes about 15% less damage than mid gear.

where: GR-4, whose band step of +17% is derived from it

assumptions.reason: It caps how much gear can matter. That is the very thing the reset wants reopened for an exciting gear chase.

assumptions.paraphrase: Early Access holds 120 days of grounds and each region opens 30 days before the first parties arrive.
assumptions.reason: A content budget derived from LP-1 and LP-2.

assumptions.paraphrase: The training yard pays a flat rate, costs gold and no stamina, and training items are sold for gold.
assumptions.reason: The book still holds a question open only because he kept the flat rate three times in the old game.

assumptions.paraphrase: A build choice every five Levels, called Talents, designed and built with the first build.
assumptions.reason: He asked for it himself that morning. It is a new system added before the core it sits on is redesigned, so it belongs in the progression package.

assumptions.paraphrase: Two visits a day is the free game, and heroes work in town for all 12 rested hours.
assumptions.reason: Page picks on a list of seventeen. Both follow from the stamina bar (LP-10).

assumptions.paraphrase: Stamina drains one for one while hunting and refills one for one. The free bar is 8 hours and Premium is 12. Gold refills step up in price, six a day.
assumptions.reason: The session limit of the whole game and the main thing Premium sells. Nobody has asked whether a limit on hunting hours is the right limit.

assumptions.paraphrase: The Bestiary's kill stages and its bonus, and the Luck bar with its ruled hours.
assumptions.reason: He queued a Bestiary deep dive himself on 2026-11-11. The reset lists the Bestiary for review.

assumptions.paraphrase: The first regions as built: the Mill Cellar start, the Sewer from Level 5, and the grounds up to Krell's Hold at Level 88 to 110.

where: guard cells keyed by ground name in tests/balance-guard.baseline.json

assumptions.reason: Existing content. The first hour of the new game is already scripted around these rooms.

assumptions.paraphrase: A region is about 55 Levels, six grounds and two bosses, with the last boss in a keyed hall.
assumptions.reason: An authoring shape. It should follow the progression curve and not precede it.

assumptions.paraphrase: The Burning Tower: its own mode, about half of hunting XP, six keys a hero a week, chest odds, and weapons with plus skill.

where: tests/tower-chest.mjs and four more tower tests

assumptions.reason: A built feature with many ruled details. It must earn its place as endgame.

assumptions.paraphrase: The Catacombs: its own mode with wings, key families and checkpoints.
assumptions.reason: Mostly unbuilt. It was kept by the rule that nothing planned is cut (PL-6).

assumptions.paraphrase: Boss rules: a paid boss call that can drop an item, and Krell as a daily kill. The overhaul folds both into keyed halls.
assumptions.reason: The daily Krell kill began as a remark with a maybe in it and is printed in the book as a ruling.

assumptions.paraphrase: An old ground can be hunted at the leader's Level, bought by the hour.
assumptions.reason: One answer to keeping old grounds useful. Others were not compared.

assumptions.paraphrase: How a ground is put together: uneven spawn mixes, one rare carrier, routes through real space, and passive mining and woodcutting between pulls.
assumptions.reason: Authoring rules of the current engine.

assumptions.paraphrase: Two factions, mostly cosmetic, with aligned grounds and one faction skill each.
assumptions.reason: A social system added late to the old game. It is on the reset's list as a social system.

assumptions.paraphrase: The story and its names: Havora, the Barrow March, Lord Krell and the named characters.
assumptions.reason: The reset is about systems and math. Story and names fit any system design and nothing asks to redo them, but they bind no system either.

assumptions.paraphrase: Klappa's Klub stays in the game under that name.
assumptions.reason: An owner's personal requirement in unconditional words. It costs the design nothing. Its stats and place are free.

words.text: it CANNOT be removed from the game

assumptions.paraphrase: Seven material tiers worn from Levels 1, 15, 30, 45, 60, 75 and 88. Past tier 7, unique pieces on a gear curve with bands about 17% apart.
assumptions.reason: The reset says item tiers must earn their place. The overhaul kept all seven and fitted a curve through them.

assumptions.paraphrase: A major gear upgrade comes every 15 to 25 Levels and is worth 5 to 8%. An armor upgrade is worth 3 to 5% less damage.
assumptions.reason: This is the flat percent step that the 2026-11-21 gear requirement calls dull.

assumptions.paraphrase: Drop cadence: a Rare about once in 10 to 20 hunted hours and a Very Rare far less often. Generous drops to Krell, rare and strong after. One base drop chance for everyone.
assumptions.reason: Rates chosen for fixed gear. Randomized gear changes what a drop is worth, so the cadence must be found again.

assumptions.paraphrase: No bound gear, so every piece trades. Gear is gated by hero Level only. No gear for reaching a Level.
assumptions.reason: It defines the economy and the paid edge. A strong preference to confirm in the economy package.

assumptions.paraphrase: The upgrade stack: Tempering, Hallmarks at typed fees, linings and curing slots. The sinks are priced above what a band earns on purpose.
assumptions.reason: Three stacked upgrade systems that each add a percent. The reset asks which features add complexity without enough value.

assumptions.paraphrase: The crafting trades and who makes what: Smithing makes all jewelry, Crafting makes cloaks and belts, with Runecrafting, Cooking, Farming and the gathering skills.
assumptions.reason: The reset names crafting professions for review. The overhaul refined each trade and questioned none.

assumptions.paraphrase: The itemization plan of 2026-11-18 is a source of record for every review and plan.

where: later lanes FR-6, FR-8 and FR-9

assumptions.reason: A document was given authority as a whole. Its fixed-stat base is now superseded (IT-1).

assumptions.reason: His wish here points the same way as the new gear requirement. The built form (one fixed property a piece) is the old answer.

assumptions.paraphrase: Loot rules for each item (keep, store, sell, use as supply), with salvage as a fourth line.
assumptions.reason: Handling rules. They follow the item design.

assumptions.paraphrase: No hunt ever starts by itself. The player picks what a hero does when a hunt ends.

assumptions.reason: A Premium perk of the old game.

assumptions.paraphrase: Profit is reported and never used to tune a hunt.

assumptions.paraphrase: The list of gold sinks and their typed prices: the bench tax, priced setup slots, rename fees, Town Works, colored fuels and more.

claudeMdLines.line: Server-authoritative, online only, hunts run on the server, the server owns shared value, no back-compat
claudeMdLines.note: Core vision and real technical limits.

claudeMdLines.line: Grow content by adding data rows, not code
claudeMdLines.note: The same rule as shared mechanics.

claudeMdLines.line: The game designer is the final design authority, and there is no approval wait
claudeMdLines.note: Conflicts with requirement R-8. It needs Tyler's word to change, because an agent may not edit this file.

claudeMdLines.line: The designer rules keep, fix, merge or cut for each system, and Tyler approves cuts
claudeMdLines.note: The package review of R-8 replaces it for the redesign.

claudeMdLines.line: Combat-engine changes are batched by the world-tick parity rule
claudeMdLines.note: A release rule for today's engine. It is not a design limit.

claudeMdLines.line: One combat engine runs every hunt, the same online and offline
The engine file, the 10 second settle and the 100 millisecond steps
claudeMdLines.note: Facts about today's code written as invariants.

claudeMdLines.line: A death costs 6% of Level XP and of combat skill progress, with Blessings at 25, 50 and 75%
claudeMdLines.note: A balance number inside the persistence rules. It is the clearest case of tuning written in as law.

claudeMdLines.line: One account for each player, with up to four character sessions
claudeMdLines.note: An implementation choice that now sets the unit of play.

claudeMdLines.line: Prototypes are frozen and the game is the source of truth
claudeMdLines.note: True for code. For design, the reset makes the game as built one input and not the truth.
